new.doc: A face shrunk to its trims (`SmFace::ShrinkGeometry`) keeps its trim curves where its surface's trim keeps the surface's parameterization by construction (`SmSurface::TrimKeepsParameterization`, asked before the trim): a B-spline surface always (its patch is extracted by knot insertion), a cone, cylinder, sphere, torus or surface of revolution where the rotation's range stays as it is and the generator is untrimmed or a line, and no other kind.
`SmBSplineSurface::SwapUV` keeps an analytic surface's definition as it was made (`SwapUVDefinition`).
`SmFace::ShrinkGeometry` takes a face-domain bound within 64 ulp of one of its B-spline surface's knots (`64 * DBL_EPSILON * |knot|`) as that knot, before the trim.

`SmApiOffsetBrepFull` and `SmApiShellBrepFull` (offset, shell and thicken) run `SmBrep::ValidateAndUpdateTolerances(FALSE)` on their result before returning it, so its vertex and edge tolerances cover the gaps its construction left and it passes the check without the caller running the update.
Unbounded `SmCone`s are parameterised as their NURB is (WR-713, #2313).

Not upstream (WR-710, #2256): `SmFilletCorner::Create` refuses a 3x2 mixed-convexity corner (`SmFillet3x2MixedConvexityCorner`: three edges at the vertex, two filleted, one convex and one concave) whose two filleted edges leave the vertex along one tangent in the same sense (a bar's front top edge and the concave arc where its top meets a cylinder that its front face runs tangent into).

`SmPolarConversion::SetUpPolarConversion` (an ellipse's polar converter) takes an open arc's end angles as its ends' own polar angles (`atan2(rx / ry * y, x)` in `[0, 360)`); `STEPInversion` over the temporary full circle, whose seam rule takes a point within tolerance of 360 for 0, is kept for an arc whose NURB is closed.

`SmTopologyIntersector::IntersectInsertRelate`, before `ResolveIntersections`, removes the edge definition of two planar faces' crossing line (and its proto edge when that is left without one) when both sides of the crossing are bounded by edges of the two faces running straight and parallel to the crossing, covering it, facing it (`binorm.dot(off) < 0`) and lying within the edge/face intersection tolerance of the opposite plane (with at least one side represented by an edge-on-face definition): the planes then stay within tolerance of each other across the whole strip where both faces exist, and the crossing, fixed only to `tol / sin(angle)`, is not an edge.

A boss or a cut whose footprint is an inner loop of a face a round rolls on, and which the round's band reaches, stays: the round runs its whole edge, the feature's walls are carried to it and it is trimmed there in place, instead of the merge dropping the feature (WR-703, the fork's eb883ad; `blend::fillet_executive::session::keep_features`).

With [`Self::fillet_gn_section_generator`] also on (a no-op otherwise): constant and variable-radius rounds between NURBS faces are built as their definition, a [`crate::surface::procedural_blend::ProceduralBlend`] (the fork's `SmProceduralBlend`): the two faces the ball rolls on, its radius or radius law, the section's order and thumbweight rule and the leader, which evaluate exactly; its net, the certified B-spline approximation within the certificate's bound (the radius law in the certificate), is what the surface cache and tessellation use (`SmBlendNetScope`), the cache's node boxes grown by the net's bound.

The fork's blend corner (`SmBlendCorner`, smlib#79 step 4b; WR-697): two blends of one convexity among three or four edges at a vertex are classified as a Join (their edges continue each other, or meet at 5 degrees or less at a face corner of the other convexity) or a Turn, and built by the two-blend construction pinned SMLib's `SmFilletNx2Corner` has, unchanged (the fork's 74e9beb and 48a8a9f, bit for bit as before).

The executive's circular rounds (`SetFilletParameters` with `SM_FSG_CIRCULAR`, and the corners' constant rounds, `SmFilletCorner::MakeConstantRadiusFillet`) take the ball's exact rational circle as their section, not polynomial arcs within 0.05% of the radius; an explicit request for approximated arcs (the cross-section type of `SmApiConstantRadiusFillet`'s options) keeps them.

With `fillet_exact_arc_sections`, the exact circular sections of one round (`SmCircularCrossSectionFSG::CreateSurfaceFromCurves` with `bApproximateArcs` FALSE) all take the largest arc count among them.

With [`Self::fillet_round_as_definition`] (and [`Self::fillet_gn_section_generator`]) also on (a no-op otherwise): a round of one radius on a face that is itself a round of one radius between NURBS faces by its definition is built as its definition, two deep.

With `fillet_cliff_overflow` (and its prerequisites), a blend past its faces is trimmed at its creases where it is built instead of being closed into the region it removes and subtracted (the fork's `SmFilletExecutive::TrimAtCreases`, `SmFilletOverflow.cpp`, tangency-labs/smlib#79 step 6 at 5e8c9c1, which deletes `SubtractRemovalRegion`): the open ends are cut by their end faces' planes as before; each sheet face is sectioned by every body face near it that holds none of its boundary, exactly by a plane, and split along each crease where it lies inside both faces; a piece is kept only when its inner point lies inside the body; a planar support face whose kept rail runs past its boundary into the material is carried on along its plane to the rail; the kept sheet's boundary is imprinted on the body's faces, the faces it encloses round the blended edges are deleted, the sheet is merged in and stitched, the body oriented, and the edges between faces sewn in on one surface removed.

With both `fillet_overflow_trim_at_creases` and `fillet_round_ends_at_tangent_continuation`, a round with a section end (WR-674: its filleted edge runs on tangentially at the vertex) is trimmed at its creases and sewn into the body as a cliff overflow is, instead of being closed into the region it removes and subtracted: each section end is cut by its plane through the vertex normal to the filleted edge and given its flat end face (the section's corner, from the section's ends to the vertex), and the sheet is trimmed and sewn in as `fillet_overflow_trim_at_creases` does it; a side of an end face that lies along an edge of the body (the seam where a corner's cylinder runs on tangentially into a flat side) is sewn to that edge's piece instead of being imprinted.

With `fillet_overflow_trim_at_creases`, a crease of a blend past its faces that runs along an edge of the face it crosses, within the trim's tolerance, is taken as that edge: the sheet is split along it, its piece past the face is deleted, and the body's edge stands as the imprint where the material taken off stops and the sheet is sewn (as an extension's edges along the body do).

With `fillet_gn_section_generator`, a convex blend whose section between its rails would break through the part (leave its material through a face and come back into it, where one of the faces it crosses there shares no edge with the blended faces: a hollow behind a wall, such as a round on a wall thinner than it reaches into the hollow behind, or a blind pocket or cavity under a blended face, which the pinned construction builds into a body that intersects itself or has the wrong volume) is refused with `FilletErrorType::NoRoom` (`NoRoomReason::BreaksThrough`), naming the largest size whose sections do not break through, and that size less the fit margin is the refusal's fit (`SolidError::FilletRefused`).

`SmPlane::GlobalSurfaceIntersect` with a torus as the other surface takes the torus's own plane section (`SmSurfOfRevolution::IntersectWithPlane` with the torus's iso circles: the circles of a plane square to the axis, the meridians of a plane through it), the orders and UV curves swapped as for a surface of revolution, where upstream has no torus case and marches it (circles 1.4e-6 off, meridians 3.5e-6 off); a meridian keeps its generator's circle kind (WR-721, #2405; solidcore-native, no fork commit).

A face made from exact pcurves keeps them as its edge uses' trims where upstream drops them and projects each edge's curve again later, a fit: the draft extrusion's curvature-keeping and tangent-plane walls ([`crate::primitive::primitive_creation::p2::PrimitiveCreationAccess::face_with_curves`]) pass theirs to `SmBrep::MakeFaceWithCurves` with `pbOptCrvOnSurf` set, and `SmBrep::CopyFaces` without the merge passes a face's own trims (`CreateCurvesFromFace`) on to its copy.
Shell, offset and thicken as one construction (tangency-labs/solidcore#2350; solidcore-native, no fork commit; WR-718).
